presentation.label: SPECTRUM
presentation.summary: A live spectrum analyzer on the pedal screen, 40 Hz to 16 kHz, with peak hold.
presentation.overview: Spectrum shows what reaches its slot as 126 log-spaced bars from 40 Hz to 16 kHz with peak hold, up to about 30 times a second, and passes the audio through untouched. Range sets how far below full scale it shows, Fall how fast the bars drop, and Tilt lifts the highs so pink noise reads flat.
highlights: 126 bars from 40 Hz to 16 kHz with peak hold
Range, fall speed and tilt to read it your way
usage: Put Spectrum last in a patch to see what the chain sends out.
Play: the bars show 40 Hz to 16 kHz, with the peaks held above them.
Range sets how far below full scale it shows, Fall how fast the bars drop, Tilt lifts the highs.

access.location: The pedal's effect list, Delay group, as Spectrum.
steps: Add Spectrum to a patch from the effect list (Delay group).
Its knobs are on the effect's pages, three per page.

controls.name: Range
controls.doc: Shown range below 0 dBFS: 30 to 90 dB.

controls.name: Tilt
controls.doc: Lifts the highs: 0 to 6 dB per octave around 1 kHz, so pink noise reads flat at the default.

limitations: Its live screen needs the MS-70CDR 2.10.
Built with the init path off: a recalled patch plays the knobs' defaults until you touch a knob.

load.conditions: The cost Spectrum declares in its descriptor, which the pedal adds up per patch; not read from the DSP meter.

hardware.summary: The release file was on the pedal (read back over USB with the same SHA-256): the pedal booted, the effect showed its screen and did its job.
limitations: One run, reported by the tester as working; nothing measured.
Built with the init path off: the sound takes saved knob values only once a knob is touched.
MIDISTOMP V2.0.1 on Zoom's 2.10, not Zoom's 2.10 alone.

tests.summary: The release file has no code from Zoom's effects (check_no_stock.py), passes Ziddle's loader check, renders in Ziddle, and ran on an MS-70CDR.
